How it worksWhy block storagePricing
How it works

Storage in three steps

Block storage is decoupled from your server: create it once, then attach, detach, and move it as your needs change.

  1. 1

    Create a volume

    Pick a size in the dashboard and provision an NVMe-backed volume in seconds. You only pay for the capacity you create.

  2. 2

    Attach it to a VPS

    Connect the volume to any of your servers with one click. Move it between servers whenever you need to, no rebuild.

  3. 3

    Mount & use it

    Format and mount the block device like any disk, then store databases, media, backups, or anything that outgrows the OS disk.

Why block storage

Separate your data from your server

When storage and compute scale independently, you stop over-provisioning, and your data stops being tied to a single machine.

Add space without resizing

Attach more storage to a server without touching its vCPU or RAM. Add another volume when you need more space instead of over-buying a bigger box up front.

Data survives detach

Detach a volume and your data stays intact. Re-attach it to the same or a different VPS later and everything is exactly where you left it.

NVMe-backed

Volumes live on the same enterprise NVMe as our servers: real IOPS for databases, build caches, and heavy read/write workloads.

Portable between servers

Because storage is decoupled from compute, a volume can follow your workload. Rebuild a server and re-attach the same data in seconds.

OS disk stays protected

Snapshots continue to protect your server’s OS disk separately, so your system image and your data volumes are each covered.

Pay for what you provision

Flat {{nxm:price}} per GB per month, billed from your wallet. No tiers, no minimums: scale up or down and the bill follows.

Pricing

One rate: {{nxm:price}} per GB / month

No tiers and no minimums: multiply your GB by {{nxm:price}} and that’s the monthly cost. Pay only for what you provision.

For the status page, I'm planning the loader to pull health data, uptime summary, timelines, and incidents, then render server-side HTML fragments for the overall status card, components, and incidents sections. I'll also add a lightweight refresh script that polls the page every 15 seconds and swaps in the updated live status markup.

I'm working out the styling details: reusing the homepage's status-card glow effect with a `--k` color variable (amber for degraded, red for down), plus dot indicators with warn/bad color states, an auto-refreshing pill with a pulsing dot, and a "last checked" timestamp shown in the swapped content.

For the layout, the hero area places the overall status as an h1 inside the status card, with a small "System status" pill above it, keeping things minimal. Incidents render as cards with a severity dot, title, body, meta info, and a resolved/active chip, with an empty state for when there's no history.

I also want an "About this page" note card, and I'm checking that timestamps render cleanly using locale formatting with a UTC suffix, plus confirming the "Days" label pulls from the uptime window constant.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

input.message:
All seven deliverables are built and render 200 on :3033: /nxm/developers, /features, /vibe-coding, /block-storage, /status, /help, and the /nxm 404. The whole-project typecheck shows 0 errors outside `.next/types`, and the port audit reports every page "wired" (or "static" for developers and the 404) with no stale prices. No commits, no deploys; screenshots are small PNGs in /tmp only.

**The five pages built before the outage.** Screenshots at 1440 and 390 show no horizontal overflow. Each is a native page using the same shell as about/security: hero with pill and gradient h1, `gp-head` sections, `au-card`/`au-glass` grids, the design's `.layers` list and `wh-final` close.
- **/developers** — static copy from the live page.
  - Visual is the homepage's developer terminal showing the live curl/JSON sample; the command types once in view, then the response appears.
  - Live/Soon availability shows as chips on the cards and scopes.
- **/features** — the live page's 18 feature cards and specs.
  - The "Location" spec comes from `liveRegions()` (currently "Germany or Singapore, low latency across Europe and APAC").
  - The Claude flagship sits on the Matrix wallpaper stage (package `mx/wp_isles.webp` + `logos/claude.svg`); its build steps tick through once in view.
  - Changed from live: the mock's "Live at https://your-bakery.nxeon.app" became "Running on your server". The live /vibe-coding FAQ says there is no automatic subdomain or certificate, so the live line contradicted it.
- **/vibe-coding** — the live `VibeCodingLanding` content plus the page's own sections.
  - Hero demo types the prompt, shows the build lines, then the site appears; it runs once, not looped. The stack marquee became static chips.
  - Sign-in path toggle, reasons bento, laptop-vs-VPS table and FAQ are the live copy. FAQPage JSON-LD is generated from the FAQ markup.
  - Pricing teaser uses three real plans from `vpsPlans()` (the live picks: first, middle, last) with real `deployHref` links; intro price shows only when a plan has one.
  - The "Browse N ready-made prompts" count is `PROMPTS.length` from `lib/ai-build`.
  - Testimonials show only if the admin has published some (none currently). The live illustrative fallback was dropped under the no-invented-reviews rule.
  - Wording change: "Claude Code, Anthropic's real command-line tool" instead of "the real Anthropic CLI", and the FAQ says "same Claude Code". The registry keeps the live SEO description, which still contains "the real Anthropic CLI".
- **/block-storage** — every price comes from `volume_price_cents_per_gb`, as you confirmed.
  - That covers the hero mock's volume costs, the 50/100/500 GB examples and the meta description (via `meta()`).
  - Adds Product JSON-LD with a per-GB UnitPriceSpecification.
- **/status** — the live readers (`getHealth`, `overallStatus`, `uptimeSummary`, `allTimelines`, `listIncidents`) and the `lib/status-copy` wording.
  - The headline reuses the homepage status band (`.status-card`), coloured by overall state.
  - Each component gets a 90-day strip; days with no data are grey, and null uptime reads "No history yet".
  - Incidents and the empty state use the live copy.
  - Auto-refresh re-fetches this same page every 15s and swaps the `#st-live` region, pausing while the tab is hidden, so no JSON endpoint is exposed. I tested it: the region was replaced after a refresh.

**/help**
- Data comes from `getHelpData()`: all published guides (33 on staging), grouped by category.
- The real `?q=` search and `?c=` topic filter work, including the "Nothing found" state with a link to /contact.
- Articles link to /nxm/blog/<slug>. Category marks are design icons instead of the live emoji.
- `meta()` keeps the canonical at /help and sets noindex for filtered or search variants. Popular articles get ItemList JSON-LD.

**404**
- `app/nxm/not-found.tsx` renders the native `not-found` page: nav, a big 404, a real search (the help center's), home and dashboard buttons, and links to VPS, game servers, web hosting, email, domains, pricing, help, blog, status and contact.
- It is generated by my own `tools/nxm/port_notfound.py`. That runs the unchanged `port_pages.port()` pipeline without writing a route, so no soft-404 page exists at /nxm/404, and it rewrites `scripts.ts` exactly as port_pages does.
- Verified 404 status with the native page for: `/nxm/blog/no-such-post-xyz`, `/nxm/mods/minecraft/no-such-mod-xyz`, and `/nxm/zzz-missing` (the other agent's `[slug]` catch-all calls `notFound()`).
- I did not add `[...rest]`, and it isn't strictly needed. The only gap: deeper unmatched paths like `/nxm/a/b/c` fall through to the old root 404. If you want those covered, the owner of `[slug]` could add `app/nxm/[slug]/[...rest]/page.tsx` that just calls `notFound()`.

**Things to know**
- **Class-name collision:** the design's homepage CSS already defines `.hc-ch`, `.hc-ic` and `.hc-title`. My first help version used `.hc-ch` and the category headers rendered as a vertical strip; renamed to `.hc-cath` and fixed. I checked all my prefixes (`k- dv- ft- vb- bs- st- hc- nf-`) and found no other collisions.
- **Hydration warning:** one 390 run logged a hydration mismatch pointing at the shared `MarketingFooter` accordion (`<details className="group py-4">`). It didn't reproduce on rerun (about and features both clean), so it's likely dev-server recompile timing, not these pages.
- **Review badges:** on /vibe-coding at 390 they render as name-only chips. That styling comes from the shared `nxm-reviews` component, not my page.
- **Live claims kept as-is that don't match the code:**
  - /developers lists scopes `servers:write`, `storage:write`, `billing:read`, but the token UI (`lib/actions-tokens.ts`) offers only `read`/`write`.
  - The API example shows `nxe_live_…` while real tokens are `nxe_<prefix>_…`.

**Files (all mine)**
- `tools/nxm/native/{developers,features,vibe-coding,block-storage,status,help,not-found}/` (body.html, page.css, page.js where needed, meta.json)
- `tools/nxm/wire/{developers,features,vibe_coding,block_storage,status,help,not_found}.py`
- `tools/nxm/port_notfound.py`
- `app/nxm/_data/{features,vibe-coding,block-storage,status,help}.ts`
- `app/nxm/not-found.tsx`
- Generated: `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/*`, `app/nxm/{developers,features,vibe-coding,block-storage,status,help}/page.tsx`, and `app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts` (regenerated, lists every page)

**Shared-file edits**
- `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py`: 6 ROUTES lines.
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: 6 entries with the live titles and descriptions; block storage's registry description has no price, since `meta()` supplies the priced one.

**Screenshots** are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/`:
- 1440: `dv-p*`, `ft-p*`, `vb-p*`, `bs-p*`, `st-p*`, `hc-p*`, `nf-p0`
- 390: `m-dv-p*`, `m-ft-p*`, `m-vb-p*`, `m-vb-hero.png`, `m-bs-p*`, `m-st-p*`, `m-hc-p*`, `m-nf-p0`

**Owner decisions**
1. Keep the live illustrative testimonials on /vibe-coding when none are published, or keep the new behaviour of showing nothing?
2. Accept the reworded bakery mock line on /features?
3. Correct the /developers scope list and token prefix to match the real token system, or keep them as the live page has them?

All seven pieces are built and load on the staging dev server:
- `/nxm/developers`
- `/nxm/features`
- `/nxm/vibe-coding`
- `/nxm/block-storage`
- `/nxm/status`
- `/nxm/help`
- the new site's 404 page

The typecheck is clean, and the price audit passes on every page. Nothing is committed or deployed.

**What each page pulls from the system:**
- **Features:** where servers run comes from the regions that actually have servers enabled.
- **Vibe coding:** three real VPS plans with real deploy links, and the number of ready-made prompts from the dashboard's prompt library.
- **Block storage:** every price comes from the block-storage price setting, the one a volume order actually charges.
- **Status:** the live health checks, 90 days of uptime per component, and incident history. It refreshes itself every 15 seconds. A component with no recorded history says "No history yet" instead of assuming 100%.
- **Help:** all 33 published guides, with the same search and topic filter as the live page.

**The 404 page** shows the site nav, the help-centre search and links to the main pages. I checked it on a missing blog post, a missing mod and an unknown single-segment address. Deeper unknown addresses like `/nxm/a/b/c` still fall through to the old site's 404. Covering those would need a small extra route under the other agent's `[slug]` folder; I didn't add one.

**What I changed from the live pages:**
- **Features:** the demo chat used to end with "Live at your-bakery.nxeon.app". The live vibe-coding FAQ says there's no automatic subdomain, so it now says "Running on your server".
- **Vibe coding:** "the real Anthropic CLI" is now "Anthropic's real command-line tool". The search description in the SEO registry still has the old wording.

**Checks:** I screenshotted every page at 1440 and 390 wide, with no sideways scrolling. At 390, the vibe-coding hero demo overflowed its frame; I fixed it and rechecked.

**Decisions for the owner:**
1. **Testimonials on vibe coding:** none are published yet, so the section is hidden. The live page instead shows made-up example use cases, labelled as illustrative. Keep it hidden, or bring those back?
2. **Features demo:** accept the reworded chat line above?
3. **Developers page:** it lists four token permissions and a sample key starting `nxe_live_`. The real system only offers read and write, and real keys don't start that way. Should the page match the system, or stay as the live page has it?

All page source is under `tools/nxm/native/` in the worktree, and the screenshots are in my scratchpad folder.
